dimensions.assessment: Affects Medicare beneficiaries, health care providers, and third-party contractors in New Jersey, Ohio, Oklahoma, Texas, Arizona, and Washington.
dimensions.evidence: The CMS selected six states to participate in this model over a six-year period: New Jersey, Ohio, Oklahoma, Texas, Arizona, and Washington.

dimensions.assessment: Stops a federal pilot program utilizing third-party contractors and enhanced technology for prior authorization of Medicare claims.
dimensions.evidence: such rule shall have no force or effect

dimensions.assessment: Halts a payment model where contractors are paid based on a share of resulting savings from claim reviews across six states.
dimensions.evidence: Contracted companies are paid based on the share of resulting savings.

dimensions.assessment: Exercises congressional disapproval authority under chapter 8 of title 5 to nullify a specific CMS program rule.
dimensions.evidence: providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services

dimensions.assessment: Permanently terminates the six-year regional Medicare pilot model.
dimensions.evidence: such rule shall have no force or effect

missing_information: Exact monetary savings or administrative costs of the halted model are not quantified.
importance_detail.rationale: The joint resolution expresses congressional disapproval under the Congressional Review Act to halt a CMS pilot prior authorization model for select Medicare services in six states.
